people.name: Abhimanyu
people.epithet: Son of Arjuna and Subhadrā
people.description: Abhimanyu, son of Arjuna and Subhadrā, dies heroically in the cakra-vyūha on the thirteenth day of battle.

people.name: Aditi
people.epithet: Mother of the Ādityas
people.description: Aditi, daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Kaśyapa, is mother of the Ādityas — including Indra and Vivasvān.

relationships.note: Named among Ādityas in Purāṇic lists.

people.name: Aja
people.epithet: Son of Raghu; father of Daśaratha
people.description: Aja, son of Raghu, is father of Daśaratha in the Solar/Raghu genealogy.

people.name: Ambālikā
people.epithet: Mother of Pāṇḍu (by niyoga)
people.description: Ambālikā, widow of Vicitravīrya, bears Pāṇḍu through Vyāsa's niyoga.

people.name: Ambikā
people.epithet: Mother of Dhṛtarāṣṭra (by niyoga)
people.description: Ambikā, widow of Vicitravīrya, bears Dhṛtarāṣṭra through Vyāsa's niyoga.

people.name: Ananta
people.epithet: Endless serpent; bed of Viṣṇu
people.description: Ananta (Śeṣa) is the foremost Nāga, son of Kaśyapa and Kadrū. He supports the worlds and serves as Viṣṇu's couch.

people.name: Anasūyā
people.epithet: Wife of Atri; mother of Dattātreya
people.description: Anasūyā is the wife of Atri, celebrated for chastity and austerity; Dattātreya is born to them.

people.name: Aṅgiras
people.epithet: Saptarṣi; ancestor of Bṛhaspati
people.description: Aṅgiras is a mānasaputra of Brahmā and a Saptarṣi; Bṛhaspati is born in his line.

people.name: Arjuna
people.epithet: Third Pāṇḍava; hearer of the Bhagavad Gītā
people.description: Arjuna, son of Indra through Kuntī, is the premier archer of the age and the interlocutor of the Bhagavad Gītā.

people.name: Aryaman
people.epithet: Āditya
people.description: Aryaman is named among the Ādityas in Purāṇic catalogues of Aditi's sons.

people.name: Atri
people.epithet: Saptarṣi; husband of Anasūyā
people.description: Atri is a mind-born son of Brahmā, one of the Saptarṣis, and husband of Anasūyā; through him is born Candra in Purāṇic genealogy.

relationships.note: Candra (Soma) is born of Atri in the Purāṇic lunar-line origin.

people.name: Balarāma
people.epithet: Elder brother of Kṛṣṇa
people.description: Balarāma, son of Vasudeva (born of Rohiṇī), is Kṛṣṇa's elder brother and companion in Vraja and Dvārakā.

people.name: Bali
people.epithet: Daitya king of the Vāmana episode
people.description: Bali, grandson of Prahlāda, conquered the three worlds. Viṣṇu as Vāmana requested three paces of land; Bali's gift sent him to Pātāla while honouring his vow.

relationships.note: Bāṇāsura, devotee of Śiva, son of Bali.

people.name: Bāṇa
people.epithet: Thousand-armed Daitya; son of Bali
people.description: Bāṇa (Bāṇāsura), son of Bali, is a devotee of Śiva whose conflict with Kṛṣṇa is narrated in the Bhāgavata and Harivaṃśa.

people.name: Bhaga
people.epithet: Āditya
people.description: Bhaga is listed among Aditi's Āditya sons in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa.

people.name: Bharata
people.epithet: Son of Kaikeyī; regent of Ayodhyā
people.description: Bharata, son of Daśaratha and Kaikeyī, refuses the throne won by intrigue and rules as Rāma's deputy from Nandigrāma.

people.name: Bhīma
people.epithet: Second Pāṇḍava; son of Vāyu
people.description: Bhīma, son of Vāyu through Kuntī, is the strongest of the brothers and slayer of many Kauravas including Duryodhana.

people.name: Bhīṣma
people.epithet: Son of Gaṅgā; vow of celibacy
people.description: Bhīṣma (Devavrata), son of Śaṃtanu and Gaṅgā, takes the terrible vow of celibacy so that Satyavatī's line may inherit; he is grandsire of the war.

people.name: Brahmā
people.epithet: Four-faced creator; grandfather of beings
people.description: Brahmā projects the manifest cosmos and fathers the mind-born progenitors (Prajāpatis), including the Saptarṣis of the current tradition.

variantTraditions.label: Number of Prajāpatis
variantTraditions.description: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12 lists nine mind-born sons plus Nārada; Manu Smṛti 1.34–35 lists ten; some Mahābhārata redactions list seven. Divine follows the Bhāgavata list and records variants.

relatedVerses.label: A day and night of Brahmā

people.name: Bṛhaspati
people.epithet: Preceptor of the Devas
people.description: Bṛhaspati is the guru of the Devas, born in the line of Aṅgiras.

people.name: Budha
people.epithet: Son of Candra; father of Purūravas
people.description: Budha, son of Candra (and Tārā in the Purāṇic tale), fathers Purūravas by Ilā — founding the Lunar royal line.

people.name: Candra
people.epithet: Moon; origin of the Lunar Dynasty
people.description: Candra (Soma), son of Atri in the Purāṇic account, is the celestial source of the Candravaṃśa through Budha and Purūravas.

people.name: Citraratha
people.epithet: Gandharva king mentioned in the Mahābhārata
people.description: Citraratha is a Gandharva who encounters Arjuna; the Gītā names him among Kṛṣṇa's vibhūtis.
people.notes: Parentage is not securely fixed in the primary epic passages used here; listed as a named Gandharva without invented ancestors.

people.name: Dakṣa
people.epithet: Prajāpati; father of many daughters given to Kaśyapa and others
people.description: Dakṣa Prajāpati gives numerous daughters in marriage — notably to Kaśyapa — from whom arise Devas, Daityas, Dānavas, Nāgas and other classes.

people.name: Danu
people.epithet: Mother of the Dānavas
people.description: Danu, daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Kaśyapa, is the mother of the Dānavas, including Vipracitti.

relationships.note: Listed among Danu's sons in Viṣṇu Purāṇa.
Dānava slain in Indra narratives; parentage via Danu in Purāṇic lists.
Maya the architect; counted a Dānava in epic usage.

people.name: Daśaratha
people.epithet: King of Ayodhyā; father of Rāma
people.description: Daśaratha, son of Aja, rules Ayodhyā. By Kausalyā, Kaikeyī and Sumitrā he fathers Rāma, Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna.

relationships.note: Vasiṣṭha is kulaguru of the Ayodhyā line.

people.name: Dattātreya
people.epithet: Son of Atri and Anasūyā; avatāra tradition
people.description: Dattātreya is the son of Atri and Anasūyā; later traditions revere him as a combined avatāra of the Trimūrti.

people.name: Devakī
people.epithet: Mother of Kṛṣṇa
people.description: Devakī, sister of Kaṃsa, is mother of Kṛṣṇa; Kaṃsa imprisons her after a prophecy.

people.name: Dhṛtarāṣṭra
people.epithet: Blind king; father of the Kauravas
people.description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Vyāsa and Ambikā, fathers one hundred sons by Gāndhārī, led by Duryodhana.

people.name: Diti
people.epithet: Mother of the Daityas
people.description: Diti, daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Kaśyapa, is the mother of Hiraṇyakaśipu, Hiraṇyākṣa and Siṃhikā — the root of the Daitya line.

people.name: Draupadī
people.epithet: Wife of the five Pāṇḍavas
people.description: Draupadī, daughter of Drupada, becomes the common wife of the five Pāṇḍavas after the svayaṃvara — a arrangement explained by prior boon and Vyāsa's counsel.

people.name: Duḥśalā
people.epithet: Daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī
people.description: Duḥśalā is the only daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī among the hundred-and-one siblings.

people.name: Duryodhana
people.epithet: Eldest Kaurava; rival of the Pāṇḍavas
people.description: Duryodhana, eldest son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī, leads the Kaurava side in the Kurukṣetra war.

people.name: Duḥśāsana
people.epithet: Brother of Duryodhana
people.description: Duḥśāsana, second among the Kaurava brothers, is notorious for the disrobing of Draupadī and is slain by Bhīma.

people.name: Gāndhārī
people.epithet: Wife of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; mother of the Kauravas
people.description: Gāndhārī, princess of Gandhāra, blindfolds herself and bears the hundred Kaurava sons.

people.name: Gaṇeśa
people.epithet: Lord of gaṇas; remover of obstacles
people.description: Gaṇeśa is the elephant-headed son of Śiva and Pārvatī, worshipped at the start of undertakings.

people.name: Gaṅgā
people.epithet: River goddess; mother of Bhīṣma
people.description: Gaṅgā marries Śaṃtanu and bears Devavrata (Bhīṣma), later returning to her celestial form.

people.name: Hiraṇyakaśipu
people.epithet: Daitya king slain by Narasiṃha
people.description: Hiraṇyakaśipu, son of Kaśyapa and Diti, persecuted his son Prahlāda for devotion to Viṣṇu and was destroyed by the Narasiṃha avatāra.

people.name: Hiraṇyākṣa
people.epithet: Daitya slain by Varāha
people.description: Hiraṇyākṣa, twin brother of Hiraṇyakaśipu, dragged the earth into the waters and was slain by Viṣṇu as Varāha.

people.name: Ikṣvāku
people.epithet: Founder of the Ikṣvāku (Solar) line
people.description: Ikṣvāku, son of Vaivasvata Manu, is the eponymous founder of the Solar Dynasty of Ayodhyā.

relationships.note: Many generations intervene; Raghu stands later in the Ikṣvāku line.

people.name: Indra
people.epithet: King of the Devas; an Āditya
people.description: Indra, son of Kaśyapa and Aditi, is sovereign of Svarga and foremost among the Ādityas in epic and Purāṇic narrative.

people.name: Indrajit
people.epithet: Son of Rāvaṇa; conqueror of Indra
people.description: Indrajit (Meghanāda), son of Rāvaṇa, is the foremost warrior of Laṅkā, slain by Lakṣmaṇa in the Yuddha Kāṇḍa.

people.name: Janaka
people.epithet: King of Videha; adoptive father of Sītā
people.description: Janaka of Mithilā finds Sītā in the furrow and raises her; Rāma wins her hand by stringing Śiva's bow.

people.name: Kadrū
people.epithet: Mother of the Nāgas
people.description: Kadrū, daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Kaśyapa, is the mother of the serpent race (Nāgas), including Ananta, Vāsuki and Takṣaka.

people.name: Kaikasī
people.epithet: Mother of Rāvaṇa and his siblings
people.description: Kaikasī, daughter of the rākṣasa Sumālin, is the wife of Viśravas and mother of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa and Śūrpaṇakhā.

people.name: Kaikeyī
people.epithet: Queen of Daśaratha; mother of Bharata
people.description: Kaikeyī, daughter of the Kekaya king, is mother of Bharata and the queen whose boons send Rāma into exile.

people.name: Kaṃsa
people.epithet: Tyrant of Mathurā; maternal uncle of Kṛṣṇa
people.description: Kaṃsa, brother of Devakī, usurps Mathurā and seeks to kill Devakī's children; slain by Kṛṣṇa.

people.name: Karkoṭaka
people.epithet: Principal Nāga of Kadrū's line
people.description: Karkoṭaka is named among the great Nāgas born of Kadrū in epic and Purāṇic lists.

people.name: Karṇa
people.epithet: Son of Kuntī and Sūrya; ally of Duryodhana
people.description: Karṇa is born of Kuntī and Sūrya before her marriage, raised by Adhiratha and Rādhā, and fights for Duryodhana.

relationships.note: Maternal half-brother of the Pāṇḍavas — revealed late.

people.name: Kārttikeya
people.epithet: Commander of the divine hosts
people.description: Kārttikeya (Skanda) is the war-god son of Śiva, raised by the Kṛttikās in the epic and Purāṇic accounts.

relationships.note: Some accounts emphasize the Kṛttikās as foster-mothers.

people.name: Kaśyapa
people.epithet: Progenitor of Devas, Daityas, Dānavas, Nāgas and others
people.description: Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, marries many daughters of Dakṣa. From Aditi come the Ādityas (Devas); from Diti the Daityas; from Danu the Dānavas; from Kadrū the Nāgas.

relationships.note: Indra is an Āditya, son of Kaśyapa and Aditi.

people.name: Kausalyā
people.epithet: Chief queen of Daśaratha; mother of Rāma
people.description: Kausalyā is the senior queen of Daśaratha and mother of Rāma.

people.name: Kratu
people.epithet: Saptarṣi; mind-born son of Brahmā
people.description: Kratu is a mānasaputra of Brahmā and one of the seven seers associated with the current manvantara lists.

people.name: Kṛṣṇa
people.epithet: Avatāra of Viṣṇu; speaker of the Bhagavad Gītā
people.description: Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva and Devakī, raised by Nanda and Yaśodā, is the central figure of the Bhāgavata's tenth skandha and the charioteer-teacher of the Gītā.

relatedVerses.label: I am the Self in all beings

people.name: Kubera
people.epithet: Lord of Yakṣas; half-brother of Rāvaṇa
people.description: Kubera (Vaiśravaṇa), son of Viśravas, is lord of the Yakṣas and guardian of wealth. He first ruled Laṅkā before Rāvaṇa seized it.
people.notes: Categorised as Yakṣa (lord of Yakṣas), not Rākṣasa — though of the same paternal line.

people.name: Kulika
people.epithet: Principal Nāga
people.description: Kulika is counted among the great Nāgas in traditional lists of Kadrū's progeny.

people.name: Kumbhakarṇa
people.epithet: Brother of Rāvaṇa; giant warrior of Laṅkā
people.description: Kumbhakarṇa, son of Viśravas and Kaikasī, is famed for his vast size, long sleep, and death in battle against Rāma's army.

people.name: Kuntī
people.epithet: Mother of Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna and Karṇa
people.description: Kuntī (Pṛthā), wife of Pāṇḍu, bears three Pāṇḍavas by divine fathers and earlier bore Karṇa by Sūrya.

people.name: Kuru
people.epithet: Eponym of the Kuru dynasty
people.description: Kuru gives his name to Kurukṣetra and the Kuru line; Bhīṣma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu descend in this house.

people.name: Kuśa
people.epithet: Son of Rāma and Sītā
people.description: Kuśa, twin of Lava, continues the Raghu line in later tradition after the Aśvamedha episode.

people.name: Lakṣmaṇa
people.epithet: Constant companion of Rāma
people.description: Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, accompanies Rāma and Sītā into exile and slays Indrajit.

people.name: Lakṣmī
people.epithet: Goddess of fortune; consort of Viṣṇu
people.description: Lakṣmī is the consort of Viṣṇu and the embodiment of śrī — prosperity, sovereignty and grace.

people.name: Lava
people.epithet: Son of Rāma and Sītā
people.description: Lava, son of Rāma and Sītā, is raised in Vālmīki's āśrama and appears in the Uttara Kāṇḍa.

people.name: Mādrī
people.epithet: Mother of Nakula and Sahadeva
people.description: Mādrī, second wife of Pāṇḍu, bears the twins Nakula and Sahadeva by the Aśvins.

people.name: Mahāpadma
people.epithet: Principal Nāga
people.description: Mahāpadma appears among named Nāga princes in Purāṇic lists of the serpent race.

people.name: Marīci
people.epithet: Mind-born son of Brahmā; father of Kaśyapa
people.description: Marīci is a mānasaputra of Brahmā and father of Kaśyapa, the great progenitor of many celestial lineages.

people.name: Maya
people.epithet: Architect of the Dānavas; builder of the hall at Indraprastha
people.description: Maya is the divine architect associated with the Dānava/asura side in the Mahābhārata; he builds the wondrous sabhā for the Pāṇḍavas after being spared by Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa.

relationships.note: Purāṇic lists place Maya among Danu's line; the epic treats him as Dānava/asura architect.

people.name: Mitra
people.epithet: Āditya; companion of Varuṇa in Vedic liturgy
people.description: Mitra is listed among the Ādityas born of Aditi in the Viṣṇu and Bhāgavata Purāṇas.

people.name: Nakula
people.epithet: Fourth Pāṇḍava; son of the Aśvins
people.description: Nakula, twin of Sahadeva, is born of the Aśvins through Mādrī.

people.name: Namuci
people.epithet: Dānava adversary of Indra
people.description: Namuci is a Dānava associated with Indra's battles in epic and Purāṇic memory; listed among Danu's progeny in Viṣṇu Purāṇa.

people.name: Nanda
people.epithet: Foster-father of Kṛṣṇa in Vraja
people.description: Nanda, chief of the cowherds of Vraja, raises Kṛṣṇa with Yaśodā after Vasudeva brings the infant to Gokula.

people.name: Nārada
people.epithet: Divine sage; messenger among the worlds
people.description: Nārada is a mind-born son of Brahmā, the wandering sage who transmits bhakti and often catalyzes Purāṇic narratives.

people.name: Padma
people.epithet: One of the principal Nāgas
people.description: Padma is listed among the principal Nāgas in Bhāgavata Purāṇa catalogues of Kadrū's sons.

people.name: Pāṇḍu
people.epithet: Father of the Pāṇḍavas (by divine niyoga)
people.description: Pāṇḍu, son of Vyāsa and Ambālikā, cannot father children by curse; his wives Kuntī and Mādrī invoke gods to bear the five Pāṇḍavas.

relationships.note: Born of Dharma by Kuntī's mantra.
Born of the Aśvins by Mādrī.

people.name: Parāśara
people.epithet: Father of Vyāsa
people.description: Parāśara fathers Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana Vyāsa by Satyavatī (Matsyagandhā) as told in the Mahābhārata.

people.name: Pārvatī
people.epithet: Daughter of the Mountain; consort of Śiva
people.description: Pārvatī is the daughter of Himavat and the consort of Śiva; as Śakti she is mother of Gaṇeśa and Skanda.

people.name: Prahlāda
people.epithet: Devotee-prince among the Daityas
people.description: Prahlāda, son of Hiraṇyakaśipu, remained devoted to Viṣṇu despite persecution — the paradigm of steadfast bhakti.

people.name: Pulaha
people.epithet: Saptarṣi; mind-born son of Brahmā
people.description: Pulaha is counted among Brahmā's mind-born sons and the Saptarṣis of the Vaivasvata manvantara tradition.

people.name: Pulastya
people.epithet: Saptarṣi; grandfather of Rāvaṇa
people.description: Pulastya is a mind-born son of Brahmā. Through his son Viśravas arise Kubera and the principal rākṣasas of Laṅkā.

people.name: Puloman
people.epithet: Dānava listed among Danu's sons
people.description: Puloman appears in Purāṇic lists of Danu's sons (Viṣṇu Purāṇa).

people.name: Puru
people.epithet: Ancestor of the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas
people.description: Puru, son of Yayāti, receives the kingdom; through him descend Duṣyanta, Bharata, Kuru and the Pāṇḍava–Kaurava houses.

people.name: Purūravas
people.epithet: First king of the Lunar Dynasty
people.description: Purūravas, son of Budha and Ilā, is the founding king of the Candravaṃśa; his romance with Urvaśī is classical.

people.name: Pūṣan
people.epithet: Āditya; nourisher
people.description: Pūṣan is counted among the Ādityas in Purāṇic lists of Aditi's sons.

people.name: Raghu
people.epithet: Eponym of the Raghuvaṃśa
people.description: Raghu is a celebrated Ikṣvāku king; the Raghuvaṃśa takes its name from him. Daśaratha and Rāma descend in his line.

people.name: Rāhu
people.epithet: Eclipse-graha; son of Siṃhikā
people.description: Rāhu is the son of Siṃhikā and Vipracitti. After the churning of the ocean he became an immortal eclipse-graha when severed by Viṣṇu's discus.

people.name: Rāma
people.epithet: Prince of Ayodhyā; avatāra of Viṣṇu
people.description: Rāma, son of Daśaratha and Kausalyā, is the hero of the Rāmāyaṇa — exile, the recovery of Sītā, and the establishment of rāma-rājya.

people.name: Rāvaṇa
people.epithet: Ten-headed king of Laṅkā
people.description: Rāvaṇa, son of Viśravas and Kaikasī, rules Laṅkā, abducts Sītā, and is slain by Rāma — the central antagonist of the Rāmāyaṇa.

people.name: Rohiṇī
people.epithet: Wife of Vasudeva; mother of Balarāma
people.description: Rohiṇī receives the transferred embryo and gives birth to Balarāma in the Bhāgavata account.

people.name: Rukmiṇī
people.epithet: Chief consort of Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā
people.description: Rukmiṇī, princess of Vidarbha, is taken by Kṛṣṇa from an unwanted marriage; she is foremost among his queens in the Bhāgavata.

people.name: Sahadeva
people.epithet: Youngest Pāṇḍava; son of the Aśvins
people.description: Sahadeva, twin of Nakula, is born of the Aśvins through Mādrī and noted for wisdom.

people.name: Sarasvatī
people.epithet: Goddess of speech, learning and the arts
people.description: Sarasvatī presides over speech (vāc), learning, music and the arts; she is traditionally the consort of Brahmā.

people.name: Satyavatī
people.epithet: Queen of Śaṃtanu; mother of Vyāsa and Vicitravīrya
people.description: Satyavatī marries Śaṃtanu on condition that her sons inherit. Before marriage she bore Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana Vyāsa to Parāśara.

relationships.note: Born of Parāśara before her marriage to Śaṃtanu.

people.name: Savitṛ
people.epithet: Āditya; the impeller
people.description: Savitṛ is named among the Ādityas; in some traditions he is closely identified with aspects of the solar deity.

people.name: Śambara
people.epithet: Dānava of Vedic and Purāṇic conflict narratives
people.description: Śambara is counted among Danu's sons in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa and appears as an adversary in older Indra lore.

people.name: Śaṅkha
people.epithet: Principal Nāga
people.description: Śaṅkha is named among the principal Nāgas of Kadrū's line in the Bhāgavata.

people.name: Śaṃtanu
people.epithet: King of Hastināpura; father of Bhīṣma
people.description: Śaṃtanu marries Gaṅgā and later Satyavatī; by Gaṅgā he fathers Devavrata (Bhīṣma).

people.name: Śatrughna
people.epithet: Youngest brother of Rāma
people.description: Śatrughna, twin of Lakṣmaṇa and son of Sumitrā, supports Bharata and later conquers Lavaṇa.

people.name: Śiva
people.epithet: The auspicious; lord of yoga and dissolution
people.description: Śiva is the yogi-lord of Kailāsa, consort of Pārvatī, and father of Gaṇeśa and Skanda (Kārttikeya) in the Purāṇic narratives.

variantTraditions.label: Birth of Gaṇeśa
variantTraditions.description: Śiva Purāṇa relates Gaṇeśa formed from Pārvatī's substance and later given an elephant head; Skanda Purāṇa preserves alternate tellings. Both are recorded as variants.

people.name: Siṃhikā
people.epithet: Daughter of Diti; mother of Rāhu
people.description: Siṃhikā, daughter of Diti, married the Dānava Vipracitti and bore Rāhu — a cross-lineage birth recorded in the Bhāgavata.
people.notes: Rāhu's mother is Daitya (Siṃhikā); his father is Dānava (Vipracitti).

people.name: Sītā
people.epithet: Daughter of Janaka; wife of Rāma
people.description: Sītā, found by King Janaka, marries Rāma, shares his exile, and is abducted by Rāvaṇa — the moral centre of the Rāmāyaṇa.

people.name: Subhadrā
people.epithet: Sister of Kṛṣṇa; wife of Arjuna; mother of Abhimanyu
people.description: Subhadrā, sister of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, marries Arjuna and bears Abhimanyu.

people.name: Sumitrā
people.epithet: Queen of Daśaratha; mother of Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna
people.description: Sumitrā is mother of the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna.

people.name: Śūrpaṇakhā
people.epithet: Sister of Rāvaṇa
people.description: Śūrpaṇakhā, daughter of Viśravas and Kaikasī, encounters Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa in the Daṇḍaka forest — an episode that precipitates the war with Laṅkā.

people.name: Takṣaka
people.epithet: Nāga who bites Parīkṣit
people.description: Takṣaka, a principal Nāga son of Kadrū, appears in the Mahābhārata as the serpent who bites King Parīkṣit.

people.name: Vaivasvata Manu
people.epithet: Current Manu; son of Vivasvān; father of Ikṣvāku
people.description: Vaivasvata Manu, son of Vivasvān, is the Manu of the present manvantara. From him descends Ikṣvāku and the Solar Dynasty. The Bhāgavata preserves the flood narrative of this Manu.

people.name: Vālmīki
people.epithet: Ādi kavi; author of the Rāmāyaṇa
people.description: Vālmīki composes the Rāmāyaṇa and shelters Sītā; Lava and Kuśa learn the poem in his āśrama.
people.notes: Traditional accounts of his earlier life vary; parentage is not asserted here without a single primary consensus.

people.name: Varuṇa
people.epithet: Āditya; lord of waters and cosmic order
people.description: Varuṇa is counted among the Ādityas, sons of Aditi, in Purāṇic lists; he governs waters and ṛta in Vedic memory.

people.name: Vasiṣṭha
people.epithet: Family priest of the Ikṣvākus; Saptarṣi
people.description: Vasiṣṭha is a mind-born son of Brahmā, a Saptarṣi, and the kulaguru of the Solar (Ikṣvāku) kings including Daśaratha and Rāma.

people.name: Vasudeva
people.epithet: Father of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma
people.description: Vasudeva of the Yadu/Vṛṣṇi line marries Devakī; their son is Kṛṣṇa. With Rohiṇī he fathers Balarāma (transferred embryo in the Bhāgavata).

people.name: Vāsuki
people.epithet: Nāga king; rope in the churning of the ocean
people.description: Vāsuki, son of Kaśyapa and Kadrū, is the Nāga used as the churning-rope in the Samudra Manthana.

people.name: Vibhīṣaṇa
people.epithet: Dharmic brother of Rāvaṇa; ally of Rāma
people.description: Vibhīṣaṇa, son of Viśravas and Kaikasī, counsels dharma, defects to Rāma, and is crowned king of Laṅkā after Rāvaṇa's fall.

people.name: Vicitravīrya
people.epithet: Son of Śaṃtanu and Satyavatī
people.description: Vicitravīrya marries Ambikā and Ambālikā but dies childless; Vyāsa raises heirs by niyoga.

people.name: Vidura
people.epithet: Wise counsellor; brother of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu
people.description: Vidura, son of Vyāsa and a palace maid, is famed for dharma-counsel in the Mahābhārata.

people.name: Vipracitti
people.epithet: Dānava; husband of Siṃhikā; father of Rāhu
people.description: Vipracitti, a son of Danu, married Siṃhikā and fathered Rāhu.

people.name: Virocana
people.epithet: Son of Prahlāda; father of Bali
people.description: Virocana is the son of Prahlāda and father of the generous Daitya king Bali (Mahābali).

people.name: Viṣṇu
people.epithet: The preserver; source of the daśāvatāra
people.description: Viṣṇu sustains the cosmos and descends as avatāra whenever dharma declines. In the Bhāgavata creation narrative, Brahmā appears on the lotus rising from Viṣṇu's navel.

relationships.note: Brahmā emerges from the lotus of Viṣṇu's navel — a manifestation rather than ordinary birth.

relatedVerses.label: I am the Self seated in every being

people.name: Viśravas
people.epithet: Son of Pulastya; father of Kubera and Rāvaṇa
people.description: Viśravas, son of Pulastya, fathers Kubera by Ilavilā (Devavarṇinī) and Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa and Śūrpaṇakhā by Kaikasī.

people.name: Vivasvān
people.epithet: The Sun; an Āditya; source of the Solar Dynasty
people.description: Vivasvān is an Āditya, son of Kaśyapa and Aditi. Through him descends Vaivasvata Manu and the Solar (Sūryavaṃśa) line. The Gītā recalls that Kṛṣṇa taught yoga to Vivasvān.

relationships.note: Vaivasvata Manu is son of Vivasvān.

relatedVerses.label: I taught this yoga to Vivasvān

people.name: Vyāsa
people.epithet: Compiler of the Vedas; author of the Mahābhārata
people.description: Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, son of Parāśara and Satyavatī, sires Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura by niyoga for Vicitravīrya's widows.

people.name: Yadu
people.epithet: Eponym of the Yādavas
people.description: Yadu, son of Yayāti, founds the Yadu line from which Vṛṣṇi, Vāsudeva and Kṛṣṇa descend.

people.name: Yaśodā
people.epithet: Foster-mother of Kṛṣṇa
people.description: Yaśodā raises Kṛṣṇa in Gokula; the Bhāgavata recounts her maternal love and the vision of the universal form in his mouth.

people.name: Yayāti
people.epithet: Ancestor of Yadu and Puru lines
people.description: Yayāti divides his kingdom among sons; Yadu and Puru become heads of the Yādava and Paurava branches of the Lunar Dynasty.

people.name: Yudhiṣṭhira
people.epithet: Eldest Pāṇḍava; son of Dharma
people.description: Yudhiṣṭhira, born of Dharma through Kuntī, is the dharmic eldest of the five brothers and victor of the Kurukṣetra war.
